introduction.text: The Acquedotto Felice is a Renaissance aqueduct that restored water supply to Rome’s hills, symbolising the city’s modernisation under Pope Sixtus V.

history.description: Destruction of Rome’s ancient aqueducts in the 6th century left the city’s hills water‑less.
Completion of the Acquedotto Felice in 1586 by Pope Sixtus V provided a new water source for Rome’s hills.

design.description: The aqueduct spans 15 mi, running underground for 8 mi and then on arches of the Aqua Claudia and Aqua Marcia for 7 mi to its terminus at the Fontana dell’Acqua Felice.

art.description: The Fontana dell’Acqua Felice, a three‑arched mostra designed by Domenico Fontana, marks the aqueduct’s entry into Rome and serves as a public memorial to the engineering feat.
